interest: This document offers a compelling glimpse into naval coexistence and humanitarian assistance along the Yangtze River during the interwar era. It highlights an instance of cooperation where the crew of the American gunboat U.S.S. Sacramento rescued Japanese sailors from the river gunboat Simida who had fallen into the water. Additionally, it illuminates the State Department's decimal filing and cross-referencing methods, connecting Japanese internal naval affairs with records of the U.S. Asiatic Fleet.
overview: This file contains a single State Department List of Papers docket sheet for decimal classification 894.322, concerning enlisted personnel of the Japanese Navy. It records Sub No. 1, a despatch (D-577) dated December 2 sent from Willys R. Peck in Nanking to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE). The entry summarizes the rescue of three Japanese sailors from drowning by a motor sampan from the U.S.S. Sacramento after ten sailors from the Japanese gunboat Simida were thrown into the river, noting cross-references to naval files of the Asiatic Fleet.

subfiles.about: A State Department list of papers docket sheet recording an incoming despatch regarding the rescue of Japanese sailors by the U.S.S. Sacramento.
